transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Thu Feb 06 2025 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Cho (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (QuantaHealth Sec), Daniel Ortiz (QuantaHealth Cloud), Marta Gomez (QuantaHealth Procurement), Liam Reilly (QuantaHealth Legal)

Auto-summary: quick procurement intake — focus on SSO, KMS, SLA terms; customer leaning toward private keys (BYOK) but needs cost/ops analysis.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes — quick intros, then we'll run through security and procurement questions, and Elena will cover the pilot/tech plan.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Hi. Thanks. We'll probably fire through compliance questions first — we have a vendor packet to close out.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Yep totally, Marta on procurement — thanks for being here.
[00:40] Marta Gomez: Hi all. We just wanna be clear on KMS, SSO, and the SLA so we can route to legal.
[00:48] Elena Cho: Great. I'll walk through the high-level on our SSO and KMS options, then dig into how a staging pilot looks.
[00:57] Daniel Ortiz: Quick context — QuantaHealth runs Azure AD (Okta on a few teams historically). We are on a VNet with strict egress via NAT and only expect a handful of subnets to access vendor endpoints. We need specifics on IP ranges and peering.
[01:15] Marcus Li: Noted. We'll provide a network diagram and required ports. For hosted we support TLS mutual, and for private we can do VPC peering or private link - slight difference in setup time.
[01:30] Liam Reilly: From legal: what are your standard SLA uptime numbers and credits? Also retention and data deletion clauses on the DPA.
[01:40] Samir Patel: Our baseline hosted SLA is 99.9% for API availability; Dedicated has higher tiers — we can map that in the MSA. Credits are standard, but there's flexibility for enterprise terms. We'll share the SLA appendix.
[01:58] Priya Nair: On KMS — we prefer BYOK, ideally HSM-backed. Can Redwood support BYOK with customer keys stored in Azure Key Vault or do we require Redwood-managed KMS? Also curious about key rotation and exportability.
[02:20] Elena Cho: We do both. For Hosted we offer Redwood-managed keys by default; BYOK is supported via integrations with Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS. For HSM-backed keys we recommend binding via KMS integrations and we support key rotation policies. There is a small ops overhead and usually a different pricing lane.
[02:45] Daniel Ortiz: If we bring keys, is there any tokenization step where Redwood sees plaintext keys? We need assurance that keys never leave our KMS.
[02:55] Marcus Li: Short answer: no plaintext export. We use envelope encryption and only hold ephemeral wrapping keys; the customer's root key stays in their KMS. I'll follow up with an architecture note that explains the flow.
[03:15] Marta Gomez: That architecture note is critical for procurement acceptance.
[03:22] Samir Patel: We'll include that in the security pack.
[03:25] Liam Reilly: On DPA redlines — we will have a few standard asks around subprocessor notification windows and audit rights. What's your turnaround for redline review?
[03:36] Samir Patel: Usually 3–5 business days once we receive redlines, but complex exceptions can take longer; we'll flag any escalations.
[03:44] Priya Nair: Also need log retention settings and access to audit logs, ideally via the Console.
[03:50] Elena Cho: Audit logs are available in the Console for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers get a retention tier — we can increase retention for enterprise deals as an add-on.
[04:02] Daniel Ortiz: For the pilot — we want a performance baseline: 95th percentile latency for short prompts, and token cost for our typical prompt sets. Can Redwood run a runbook?
[04:18] Marcus Li: Yes, the pilot normally includes a small benchmark harness against your prompt set. We'll do 1–2 days of warm-up then a measured window. We can run it on Hosted model variants or on a Dedicated pool if you prefer to evaluate throughput guarantees.
[04:36] Marta Gomez: Pricing question — procurement needs committed usage tiers and what happens if we scale faster. Is there a ramp?
[04:46] Samir Patel: We present tiered committed discounts — there's also burst capacity available for Dedicated. We can model a ramp in the contract. I'll share the pricing scenarios.
[04:58] Priya Nair: Any export controls or data residency constraints? We host in NA and EU primarily; QuantaHealth needs EU residency for some datasets.
[05:10] Elena Cho: We have region pinning and Private deployments for strict residency. For Hosted we can route to EU-only model endpoints. For fully on-prem or VPC Private, data never leaves customer's environment if configured that way.
[05:28] Daniel Ortiz: Good. On SSO: SAML with Azure AD is fine, but we want SCIM provisioning and RBAC integrated so service accounts map to our roles.
[05:40] Marcus Li: SCIM provisioning is supported. For RBAC we support token scopes and route-level permissions — and we can map SCIM groups to Console roles. I'll prepare a mapping doc.
[05:55] Liam Reilly: Back to SLA language — do you have a template for remedies and measurement windows? Also what constitutes a breach?
[06:05] Samir Patel: We'll attach our SLA appendix that defines measurement windows, credits, and severity tiers. For breach definitions we rely on service availability metrics and escalation policies; we can work with legal to refine.
[06:22] Priya Nair: On compliance: do you publish SOC 2 report and do you allow security questionnaires?
[06:31] Elena Cho: Yes, SOC 2 Type II available under NDA; we also provide a security questionnaire pack, pen test summary, and architecture whitepaper. We'll include these in the vendor packet.
[06:45] Marta Gomez: Procurement will need cost model for BYOK vs Redwood-managed KMS — can you outline incremental fees?
[06:55] Samir Patel: BYOK can incur a per-key management fee or a flat integration surcharge depending on complexity; we'll put two sample options in the pricing sheet.
[07:08] Daniel Ortiz: Networking specifics again — do you support PrivateLink equivalents and can you provide IP ranges for allowlisting?
[07:18] Marcus Li: Yes — for public hosted endpoints we provide stable IP ranges; for PrivateLink/VPC peering we provide VPC endpoint configs. I'll send the IP list and an ops checklist.
[07:30] Priya Nair: For the pilot success criteria — what would you suggest?
[07:36] Elena Cho: We usually propose: 1) functional correctness on 5 canonical prompts, 2) latency under X ms at 95th percentile (we'll define X once we see prompt lengths), 3) throughput of Y rps for your peak flows, and 4) verification of RBAC/SSO provisioning and KMS behavior.
[07:55] Marta Gomez: That sounds reasonable. We need a 2-week runway to approve pilot spend internally.
[08:01] Samir Patel: Understood. We'll plan to start the pilot after legal signs off the DPA and procurement approves scope.
[08:10] Liam Reilly: A few redline priorities: subprocessor list updates, export control clause tweaks, and a narrower data processing scope. We'll send the initial redline.
[08:22] Samir Patel: Great — send redlines to me and copy contracts@redwood.ai and I'll route to legal. Expect our turnaround estimate in the security pack.
[08:33] Daniel Ortiz: One last technical: do you support KV cache persistence across restarts for low cold-start latencies? We have multi-turn chat workloads.
[08:45] Elena Cho: Yes, the runtime supports KV caching; persistence can be configured in Dedicated/Private deployments. In hosted there is ephemeral cache but we can do prefix caching or session pinning — we'll document expected tail latencies.
[09:02] Marta Gomez: On billing: how does committed usage get invoiced and can we do monthly true-ups?
[09:12] Samir Patel: We do monthly invoicing with committed tiers; true-ups are part of most enterprise contracts. For annual commits we offer additional discounts.
[09:25] Priya Nair: Does Redwood do code or data residency attestations for audited customers?
[09:33] Elena Cho: We can provide SOC2 and regional hosting attestations; for deeper audits we'll coordinate through the security engagement.
[09:43] Liam Reilly: Ok, we'll prepare legal redlines and confirm target SLA numbers, then circle back.
[09:50] Samir Patel: Quick recap of next steps — I'll send pricing and MSA/DPA; Elena will schedule the pilot runbook and Marcus will send network/IP docs. Customer to confirm BYOK decision.
[10:05] Marta Gomez: Thanks. That helps procurement plan.
[10:12] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[10:16] Samir Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email and attach the security pack.
[10:22] (meeting ends)
